top_choice_rationale: P003 (Helpman and Melitz, B014) credits one compact, mature discovery: productivity-sorted firms select into exporting and foreign investment, and trade reallocates resources across firms. It produced sharp predictions that firm- and transaction-level data have tested for over twenty years, and it is now standard across trade, macro and IO. The two names carry the core model (Melitz 2003) and its main extension to exports versus FDI (Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple 2004) without an arbitrary cut. Its weaknesses are real: uncredited priority claims (Bernard, Jensen, Eaton, Kortum, Hopenhayn) and the Arkolakis et al. qualification on welfare gains. A citation limited to selection and reallocation, with no claim about the size of the gains, answers the welfare point and narrows the priority point. I cannot fully resolve priority from the supplied evidence. B009 is very close on merit, so I rank it next. Its problems are in the credited object itself: whether technology and trade are one achievement or two, and whether the third name is Katz or Dorn. I put Autor-Hanson-Katz (P002) above Autor-Dorn-Hanson (P001) because a B009 prize as a whole needs Katz, though the cost of omitting Dorn is real. P004 (the BLP demand estimator) is a mature and well-attributed methods contribution. It ranks below the others because its reach is narrower and Bresnahan's claim is unresolved. No award ranks last, because every proposal on the slate rests on mature, replicated work.
recusal_note: No connection to any credited name in P001-P004 is apparent from the profile. Disclosed without adjudication: my research on pass-through, invoicing currency and pricing under imperfect competition is adjacent to P003 and P004, and I co-authored an IJIO 2026 paper with committee chair John Hassler and former chair Tore Ellingsen, neither of whom is credited. My spouse, Magdalena Andersson, is a Swedish politician (public fact only), with no apparent bearing on any proposal. I claim no independent verification beyond the supplied profile.
